name: Familial Lecithin–Cholesterol Acyltransferase Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Familial LCAT Deficiency

criteria.description: Markedly reduced or absent plasma LCAT enzyme activity
Diffuse corneal opacification visible on slit-lamp examination
Presence of proteinuria and progressive renal insufficiency
Abnormal plasma lipid profile characterized by low HDL cholesterol and accumulation of unesterified cholesterol
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of markedly reduced or absent LCAT activity plus at least two major clinical features (corneal opacities and renal involvement)
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing confirming pathogenic LCAT mutations supports diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Typically bilateral and present from early childhood

common.notes: Often the first sign of renal involvement
May progress to end-stage renal disease

searchTerms: low red blood cells from renal disease

occasional.notes: Peripheral sensory neuropathy reported in some cases

searchTerms: high blood pressure due to kidney disease

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular disease due to accelerated atherosclerosis
rare.notes: Rare but reported in older patients
searchTerms: heart disease from rapid artery hardening

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits related to ischemic events
rare.notes: Rare complication secondary to vascular disease
searchTerms: nerve problems from poor blood flow

laboratory: Markedly reduced or absent plasma LCAT enzyme activity
Elevated unesterified cholesterol and phospholipids in plasma
Proteinuria and elevated serum creatinine indicating renal impairment
imaging: Slit-lamp examination showing diffuse corneal opacities
Renal ultrasound may show increased echogenicity consistent with chronic kidney disease
other: Renal biopsy showing lipid deposits in glomerular basement membrane and mesangium

distinguishingFeatures: Partial LCAT deficiency with only alpha-LCAT activity affected
Corneal opacities without significant renal disease
Higher HDL cholesterol compared to familial LCAT deficiency
Low HDL cholesterol without corneal opacities or renal disease

redFlags: Early onset proteinuria with progressive renal failure
Bilateral diffuse corneal opacities in a young patient
Markedly reduced plasma LCAT enzyme activity
references: Calabresi L, et al. Familial lecithin:cholesterol acyltransferase deficiency: a rare genetic disorder of lipid metabolism. J Lipid Res. 2017.
Mori M, et al. Clinical and molecular features of familial LCAT deficiency. Clin Chim Acta. 2019.
